newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Airlines hurt by jet fuel rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Airlines hurt by jet fuel rise.

text.p: High jet fuel prices have been a major factor in rising expenditure for Singapore Airlines (SIA) over the last several months, deputy managing director (commercial) Michael Tan said on Friday.
"It will be a major reason for higher operating costs in the last half year," Tan said, referring to the sharply higher prices for spot jet fuel prices in Asia.
Tan was speaking to reporters during a conference announcing SIA's plans to celebrate its 50th anniversary on May 1.
He said the recent fall in crude oil prices may not have as much impact on lowering jet prices, as analysts have forecast, due to robust regional demand and seasonal factors elsewhere.
"We have seen that jet fuel doesn't necessarily move in tandem with the (crude) oil price," Tan said.
The company's financial year ends March 31.
Earlier, SIA officials had admitted that for the second half of the company's financial year, the airline had not been able to hedge as extensively as it usually does in derivatives.
This was due to expectations prices would ease as a result of renewed oil sales from Iraq, which did not occur immediately.
Jet fuel prices, down from five-year highs in December, are recapturing upward momentum and are now at US$29 per barrel.
SIA's annual jet fuel requirements are estimated at 950 million U.S. gallons or 22.62 million barrels. Fuel comprises about 10 percent of airline costs.

In December, Asian airlines raised fares by three percent in line with recommendations by the International Air Transport Association (IATA), to make up for an increase of more than 40 percent in fuel costs last year.
